Good afternoon Senator Nangle, Representative Crafts, and distinguished
members of the Transportation Committee. I am Representative Randy Greenwood, proudly representing my friends and neighbors in Litchfield, Monmouth and my hometown in Wales, both in Androscoggin and
Kennebec Counties.
I am here to testify in favor of LD 1581, "An Act Regarding the Motor
Vehicle Excise Tax Exemption for Certain Veterans" as proposed to be amended by the sponsor's amendment.
As proposed to be amended by the sponsor, this legislation would bring
Maine law in line with the intent of Title 36 �1483 (12) as amended by LD
1193 in 2021. When that change to statute was implemented, however, it
became clear that as written, the ability for 100% disabled veterans to be
exempt from motor vehicle excise tax was not limited to any specific number of vehicles.
The sponsor's amendment makes it clear that the exempt vehicles must be titled either solely to the 100% disabled veteran or jointly owned by them. Additionally, there would be a three vehicle limit for each 100% disabled veteran. Providing guardrails such as ownership and a reasonable number of
vehicles ensures against fraud and abuse, or the danger of losing this exemption for this important segment of our population.
I am asking for an Ought to Pass as Amended as agreed to and outlined by
the good Representative from Oakland, Representative Nutting.
Thank you and I am happy to take any questions you may have.

Good afternoon, Senator Nangle, Representative Crafts, and distinguished members of the Joint Standing Committee on Transportation. I am Representative Bob Nutting, and I
am proud to represent the citizens of Starks, Mercer, Smithfield, Oakland, and a part of
Sidney. I am here today to present LD 1581, "An Act Regarding the Motor Vehicle
Tax Exemption for Certain Veterans" .
In the 130th and 131st Legislatures, the law was changed about certain vehicles registered to 100% disabled veterans such that they do not have to choose to display a disabled veteran registration plate to gain the exemption on the annual registration fee
and/or the excise tax.
As a result of the changes, any vehicle with a gross vehicle weight of not more than 26,000 pounds which has such a veteran's name on the registration is exempt from both the registration fee and the excise tax. It is now possible for anyone to obtain permission from such a veteran to add his or her name to a registration to avoid all the fees and taxes Surely nobody intended for this to be true. It was an oversight or a series of oversights. I was first made aware of this oversight in August of 2024 when I received a letter from the Sidney Selectmen asking if their interpretation of the law was correct. They subsequently received in September, a letter from the Secretary of State confirming that they were correct. I was informed that in a period of three months, Sidney had lost over
$11,000.
I think that everyone believes that 100% disabled veterans deserve to be tree from
registration fees and excise taxes but not for limitless vehicles with registrations to which they have added their name.
I understand that there is at least one other bill before you (Rep. Drinkwater's LD 807)
dealing with this issue. His bill would limit the number of vehicles to three and would require the State of Maine to reimburse municipalities for the loss of excise taxes resulting in a cost to the Highway Fund of about $100,000 annually just for
administration of the program. My bill differs in that it has no limit as to the number of
vehicles and does not require the communities to be reimbursed.
District 66 Oakland, Mercer, Smithfield, Starks & Sidney (part)

My bill does, however, require that the veteran be listed on the Certificate of Title and not
simply on the registration.
Rep. Greenwood is a mandated co-sponsor on my bill because he had one which was
very similar. He asks if the veteran should be listed as a Joint Owner on the Title. I leave
that to you.
Finally, there are towns that have lost large amounts of taxes due to this loophole and I fear that it will only increase once it is more widely known. I think that tightening up this law while benefiting veterans as intended is paramount. Requiring the State to reimburse
cities and towns causes a fiscal note which may lead to the bill dying on the
appropriations table. . .perhaps that is a discussion for another legislature. . .but I ask you
to fix this oversight now with your choice of bills.
Thank you. I would be happy to take your questions.
Robert W. Nutting
State Representative
District 66 Oakland, Mercer, Smithfield, Starks & Sidney (part)

JOINT STANDING COMMITTEE ON TRANSPORTATION L.D. 1581 "An Act Regarding the Motor Vehicle Excise Tax Exemption of Certain Veterans."
Testimony of Shenna Bellows, Secretary of State and Cathie Curtis, Deputy Secretary for the Bureau of Motor Vehicles,
Department of the Secretary of State
April 17, 2025
Senator Nangle, Representative Crafts and distinguished members of the Joint Standing Committee on
Transportation, I am providing testimony neither for nor against L.D. 1581 "An Act Regarding the Motor
Vehicle Excise Tax Exemption of Certain Veterans."
We worked with Maine Municipal Association and Representatives Drinkwater, Nutting and Greenwood
to come to consensus on the amended bill that was presented by Representative Nutting earlier in this
public hearing. We appreciate the ability to weigh in on a path forward that is workable on the BMV end
and leave the policy decision-making in your hands.
As presented in the sponsor's amendment, this bill requires that for an automobile to qualify for the excise tax exemption provided in current law for certain veterans who are disabled, the name of the qualifying veteran must appear on the vehicle's certificate of title. Additionally, the number of vehicles
that may be exempted for a given person would be capped at three. The Titles Division at BMV is
capable and ready to provide municipalities the information they would need to confirm that the person seeking the excise tax exemption is on a given vehicle's certificate of title.
Thank you for your time today and I will be happy to answer any questions.
